questions.question: In 1600, the East India company acquired a charter from which ruler?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Queen Elizabeth-I
  • Charter: It gave the company a 15-year monopoly on trade with the East Indies (Asia).

questions.question: In 1526, the battle of Panipat was fought between ______.
questions.solution:
• Opponents: Babur and Ibrahim Lodi
  • Tactics: Babur used Tulughma (flanking) tactics and artillery to defeat a much larger Lodi army.

questions.question: In which among the following period Catal Huyuk was one of the most famous sites?
questions.solution:
• Period: Neolithic
  • Site: A very large Neolithic and Chalcolithic proto-city settlement in southern Anatolia (modern Turkey).

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms is mentioned in the ancient text of Vyavaharmala?
questions.solution:
• Dance: Mohiniyattam
  • Context: A classical dance from Kerala; the text provides evidence of its historical roots and evolution.

questions.question: Sultan Mahmud came to India from which of the following city of Afghanistan?
questions.solution:
• City: Ghazni
  • Legacy: He is remembered for his 17 raids on India, specifically targeting temples like Somnath.

questions.question: Which college was established in Banaras in 1791?
questions.solution:
• College: Hindu College
  • Correction: While Jonathan Duncan founded a Sanskrit College in 1791, the Hindu College was later established in 1817 (this question often refers to the Banaras Sanskrit college evolution).

questions.question: The second volume of the Akbar Nama recorded the _____.
questions.solution:
• Volume 2: Events of Akbar's reign
  • Structure: Vol 1 (Ancestors), Vol 2 (Reign details), Vol 3 (Ain-i-Akbari/Administration).

questions.question: Which of the following revolts was led by Kanhu and Sidhu?
questions.solution:
• Revolt: Santhal Revolt (1855)
  • Cause: A tribal rebellion in present-day Jharkhand against the oppression of the British and Zamindars.

questions.question: Who became the Nawab of Bengal in 1756 after the death of Alivardi Khan?
questions.solution:
• Nawab: Siraj Ud Daulah
  • Outcome: His reign led to the Black Hole tragedy and the Battle of Plassey.

questions.question: An early temple at Bhitargaon, Uttar Pradesh was built about 1500 years ago was made of _______.
questions.solution:
• Material: Baked brick
  • Fact: It is one of the oldest surviving brick temples from the Gupta era.

questions.question: Who among the following was the best-known Chahamana ruler?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Prithviraja III
  • Legacy: Popularly known as Prithviraj Chauhan, the hero of the Battles of Tarain.

questions.question: The British Parliament transferred the powers of the East India company to the British crown in ______.
questions.solution:
• Year: 1858
  • Act: Better Government of India Act; passed after the 1857 Mutiny to end Company rule.

questions.question: Who among the following is said to have devised many Raagas or melodies in Hindustani music?
questions.solution:
• Musician: Tansen
  • Context: One of the Navratnas (nine jewels) in Akbar's court.

questions.question: Vernacular press Act was enacted in which year?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1878
  • Nature: Designed to silence the Indian-language press that was critical of British policies.

questions.question: According to the archaeologists, in Harappan cities the part to the west was smaller and higher, was known as______.
questions.solution:
• Term: Citadel
  • Archeology: In Indus cities, the citadel usually contained important public buildings like the Great Bath.

questions.question: Sarojini Naidu was elected first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress at __________.
questions.solution:
• City: Kanpur (1925)
  • Note: While Annie Besant was the first woman President, Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President.

questions.question: Who among the following belonged to the ancient chiefly family of the Cholas from Uraiyur, captured the Kaveri delta from the Muttaraiyar in the middle of the ninth century?
questions.solution:
• Ruler: Vijayalaya
  • Fact: He revived the Chola power and established the dynasty that dominated South India for centuries.

questions.question: Established in 1867 at Bombay, the _________sought to remove caste restrictions, abolish child marriage, and encourage the education of women, etc.
questions.solution:
• Organization: Prarthana Samaj
  • Founder: Atmaram Pandurang; it was a movement for religious and social reform in Maharashtra.

questions.question: In 1840, the Paramhans Mandali was established to work for the abolition of ‘Caste’ at ______.
questions.solution:
• Location: Bombay
  • Context: Founded by Dadoba Panderung and Durgaram Mehta; it was a precursor to several Marathi reform movements.

questions.question: Which of the following was known as an organisation of merchants in the inscriptions of the Pallavas?
questions.solution:
• Term: Nagaram
  • Society: In the Pallava era, Nagaram specifically managed the administration of trade and commerce in towns.

questions.question: Chola inscriptions mention several categories of land, which of the following land was known as gifted to temples?
questions.solution:
• Category: Devadana
  • Meaning: Literally 'Gift to the Gods'. These lands were tax-exempt.

questions.question: Battle of Plassey was fought between English company and Nawab of Bengal in which year?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1757
  • Combatants: The English East India Company vs. the Nawab of Bengal (Siraj-ud-Daulah).

questions.question: Nagabhata was the king of which of the following dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Pratihara (Gurjara-Pratihara)
  • Ruler: Nagabhata I was the founder and saved western India from Arab invasions.

questions.question: Krishna III of Manyakheta belonged to which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Dynasty: Rashtrakuta
  • Achievement: He was a great military leader who defeated the Cholas at the Battle of Takkolam.

questions.question: Which of the following metals was used to make weapons and tools in Harappan cities?
questions.solution:
• Metal: Copper
  • Note: Harappans also used Bronze (an alloy of copper and tin). They did not know about Iron.
